title.narrative: IFU Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Investment Facility

description.narrative: Impact Fund Denmark (IFDK) is Denmark’s development finance institution, supporting sustainable private sector investments in developing countries. IFDK invests in sustainable growth and high-impact solutions, mobilising capital to tackle global challenges where the need is greatest. The focus is on investments that offer high development impact and scalable business opportunities. The Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Investment Facility was designed to contribute to IFDK’s overall objective, namely, to create economic and social development in investment countries. The purpose of the Facility was to support Danish SMEs in their internationalisation in developing countries, creating growth opportunities for Danish SMEs as well as sustainable development effects in the host countries. It also helped improve IFDK’s portfolio of SME-generated projects, increasing their chances of success and long-term development impact. Development effects often take years to materialise, making them difficult to capture within short reporting periods. As a result, the indicator reporting focuses on tangible outputs, such as the number of investments, as proxies, based on the assumption that these will contribute to long-term development impact. To learn more about the development effects, see the case stories on IFDK’s website and in IFDK’s Annual Report. Key learnings from the SME facility includes that it has been a challenge to source sufficient number of proposals from Danish SMEs that live up to the requirements of the facility. Many SMEs hold somewhat unrealistic expectations about the challenges of entering unfamiliar markets and the requirements for laying the groundwork for commercial investments, which influence the prospect for long-term sustainability (and thereby impact) of their business models. IFDK will use this learning going forward in its endeavors of keeping investing also in SMEs.

Objective: Reduced poverty by creating employment and strengthening the competitiveness and social responsibility of Danish SME-projects in developing countries.
Outcome: A quality improved IFU portfolio of SME-generated projects with higher chances of success and long term development results.
